title: In Luke 1 How Does Marys Response To The Angels Message Serve As A Model For Believers Today
paragraphs: Mary’s Response to the Angel’s Message: A Model of Faith and Surrender

The opening chapter of Luke’s Gospel introduces us to Mary, a young woman visited by the angel Gabriel with an astounding message: she would conceive and give birth to Jesus, the Son of the Most High. Mary’s response in Luke 1 offers profound lessons for believers today in how to respond to God’s calling, even when it seems impossible or overwhelming.
1. A Willing Heart Despite Fear
When Gabriel greets Mary, she is understandably troubled and afraid. The angel reassures her:
And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favor with God. - Luke 1:30 ASV

Mary’s initial fear is natural. Yet, she listens attentively to God’s messenger. For believers today, it’s encouraging to know that faith does not mean never feeling fear; rather, it means trusting God in the midst of it.
2. Honest Questions, Humble Inquiry
Mary responds with a genuine question:
And Mary said unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? - Luke 1:34 ASV

Unlike Zechariah earlier in the chapter (who questioned in disbelief; see Luke 1:18), Mary’s question arises from a place of wonder and faith, not skepticism. This distinction is important: God welcomes our sincere questions and invites us to seek understanding, provided our hearts remain open and trusting.
3. Faith in God’s Power and Promises
Gabriel explains how the Holy Spirit will accomplish the miracle and affirms God’s sovereignty:
For no word from God shall be void of power. - Luke 1:37 ASV

Mary chooses to believe God’s word, even though she could not fully grasp how it would happen. This is a key principle for believers: God’s promises are trustworthy, even when circumstances seem impossible. Faith means taking God at His word because of who He is.
4. Surrendered Obedience
Mary’s ultimate response is one of humble surrender:
And Mary said, Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. - Luke 1:38 ASV

She identifies herself as God’s servant, willingly submitting her life, reputation, and future to His plan. This is perhaps the most profound aspect of her response. For believers, Mary models the attitude described in Romans 12:1—a life offered as a “living sacrifice” to God.
5. Rejoicing in God’s Grace

Mary’s famous song, often called the Magnificat, overflows with praise for God’s faithfulness and mercy (Luke 1:46-55). She rejoices not only in her own blessing but in God’s redemptive work for all who fear Him:
My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. - Luke 1:46-47 ASV
Mary’s worship is Christ-centered and God-exalting, reminding us to give glory to God in all circumstances.
Conclusion: Mary’s Model for Believers Today
Faith over Fear: Trusting God even when afraid.
Open Inquiry: Asking sincere questions without doubting God’s character.
Confidence in God’s Promises: Believing God’s Word is powerful and true.
Surrendered Obedience: Yielding to God’s will whatever the cost.
Joyful Praise: Responding to God’s work with worship and gratitude.

Mary’s response to Gabriel is a timeless example for all believers. As we face God’s callings—both big and small—may we, too, respond: “Behold, the servant of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.”
